paper_diagnosis: Alcohol withdrawal syndrome with severe diaphoresis and fever causing hypovolemic shock and acute renal failure
disease_label_per_paper: Severe diaphoresis and fever during alcohol withdrawal cause hypovolemic shock
presentation_summary: 52-year-old man with about 20 years of alcohol use disorder, drinking about 1.5 L of wine daily, was admitted for ruptured esophageal varices and then underwent inpatient alcohol cessation.
He was fully conscious until hospital day 4, when sinus tachycardia and insomnia appeared.

On hospital day 5 he developed alcohol withdrawal signs: tremor, severe diaphoresis, tachycardia, GCS 12, visual and auditory hallucinations, moving-ceiling illusion, agitation, restlessness, and violent behavior.
On hospital day 6 he remained disoriented, restless, agitated, hallucinating, tremulous, and substantially diaphoretic; fever reached 38.9 C without evidence of infection.
On hospital day 7 he had hypotension to 75/48 mmHg with sinus tachycardia and acute kidney injury, attributed by the authors to hypovolemia from withdrawal-related diaphoresis and fever.
